title: 'People vs Palantir' protests in London and 30 UK cities over NHS contract

tea.why: Campaigners object to Palantir's £330m NHS data platform contract, citing the firm's work for militaries and US immigration enforcement.
tea.want: End the NHS contract with Palantir and other public-sector contracts with the company.
tea.changed: Oct 1: protests at about 45 locations in over 30 UK cities, the largest outside Palantir's London offices.

summary: Campaigners held a 'People vs Palantir' day of action on October 1 at about 45 locations in more than 30 UK cities, demanding an end to the US data company's £330 million contract to run the NHS Federated Data Platform. The largest protest, with hundreds of people, was outside Palantir's London offices; others took place outside hospitals, railway stations and town halls, including a group of about 50 at the Bristol Royal Infirmary. Organisers included the 'No Palantir in our NHS' campaign and Health Workers for a Free Palestine, as part of a global week of action called by the Palestinian BDS National Committee. Critics point to Palantir's work for the Israeli military and US immigration enforcement.
